title: 1980 AHSME Problem 28
statement: The polynomial \(x^{2n}+1+(x+1)^{2n}\) is not divisible by \(x^2+x+1\) if \(n\) equals

solutions.text:
Let \(\omega^2+\omega+1=0.\) Since \(1+\omega=-\omega^2,\) the polynomial evaluated at \(\omega\) is \[ \omega^{2n}+1+\omega^{4n}. \] This is \(0\) unless \(\omega^{2n}=1,\) in which case it is \(3.\) The latter occurs exactly when \(n\) is divisible by \(3.\) Among the choices only \(21\) is divisible by \(3,\) so that is the value for which divisibility fails.

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
hints: Evaluate the polynomial at a nonreal cube root of unity \(\omega\)
